messages:
taylor_sales: Hey team — Ephemeral Tide is ready to kick off a POC. They want to validate a custom model (tide-llama-adapt-14b-v2) for chat + retrieval augmentation. Main asks: can this be served on hosted Redwood or will they need Dedicated/Private? What variants are compatible (quantized 4-bit, q8_0, float16), any KV-cache issues, and ballpark pricing for ~300k tokens/day? Also they sent a security questionnaire we need answers for — cc @rachel_security :wave:

mira_se: Thanks — can you drop the model repo / sample artifact? Are the variants standard HF checkpoints or custom export? Also need to know tokenizer (sentencepiece/llama) and whether they changed lm_head.

taylor_sales: Repo -> https://github.com/ephemeraltide/tide-llama-adapt-14b (private, will share invite). They have two artifacts: tide-14b-v2.pt (fine-tuned) and tide-14b-v2-4bit.safetensors (team quantized). Tokenizer: llama tokenizer. They said they added a tiny domain-specific lm_head and a custom attention wrapper for chunking.

sashi_research: Preliminary: sounds plausible. Two red flags: (1) custom lm_head may break standard generation APIs unless exported with a compatible shape/name; (2) attention wrapper may interfere with our kernel fusion and KV-cache layout. I'll run a compatibility sweep if you can give sample weights (one shard ok).

owen_infra: For performance context — assuming avg prompt+response ~512 tokens and 300k tokens/day (peak concurrency ~10 qps), hosted can probably handle on our pooled GPUs if we serve a quantized variant. For float16 variants you'd want Dedicated to keep consistent latency. Rough throughput (RTX A6000 style): 2 replicas -> ~6–10 rps @512 tokens depending on batching. KMS: hosted supports envelope encryption; Private supports customer KMS/HSM.

lisa_eng: Quick checklist for onboarding: tokenizer file, model config (config.json), state dict, and a small sample prompt/responses for eval. If attention wrapper is in Python code only, we need an exported ONNX/TorchScript or a clear shim. To run the sweep use our internal scan tool, e.g.:

```
rdw_model_scan --model ./tide-14b-v2.pt --checks rmsnorm,kvcache,kv-layout,lm_head
```

That will report incompatible ops and a minimal conversion plan.

emma_sales_ops: Pricing notes: hosted POC ballpark — $0.08 per 1k prompt tokens & $0.12 per 1k completion tokens is a baseline for bespoke quantized variants (we can do trial credits). Dedicated quote depends on reserved GPU hours; for a 2-replica setup it's usually a fewK/month. I'll draft a range once we lock expected peak qps and retention windows.

taylor_sales: Security Qs from the customer: need SOC2, data residency in eu-west, can we guarantee no model weights leaving their VPC for Private? Also they want details on access controls for logs and eval datasets.

rachel_security: We can provide SOC2 report and an NDA addendum. For Private: yes, weights and artifacts never leave customer infra. For Hosted: we offer tenant isolation + AAD/OAuth SSO, RBAC, and audit logs; envelope encryption with CMK is available (we store logs in encrypted S3). Retention & purging: we support configurable retention policies and can run a one-time purge. I can start answering their questionnaire — please share it. :memo:

infra-bot: Compatibility scan queued for 1793456789, estimated runtime 45m. Queue position: 3.

sashi_research: Quick follow-up from initial scan (ran minimal static checks): passes RMSNorm/LayerNorm ops, but detected a nonstandard key name for `lm_head.weight` (named `domain_head.weight`) and a custom `chunk_attn` op implemented in Python. Recommendation: (1) rename/alias lm_head parameter to `lm_head.weight` during export; (2) reimplement `chunk_attn` as standard attention + pre/post-processing so RDW kernels can fuse it. Sample patch: 

```python
# patch head aliasing
state = torch.load('tide-14b-v2.pt', map_location='cpu')
state['lm_head.weight'] = state.pop('domain_head.weight')
torch.save(state, 'tide-14b-v2-rdw.pt')
```

I'll help with a minimal adapter if they share the code.

taylor_sales: Awesome, can we get timeline? Client wants POC spin-up next week.

mira_se: If they share a single example shard + tokenizer today, I can run a full compatibility/latency sweep and smoke tests in ~48–72 hours. If we need to rebuild kernels or re-export, add another 2–4 days.

emma_sales_ops: I'll put together a hosted POC quote + a Dedicated starter quote and include trial credits. Sending draft by EOD.

taylor_sales: Thanks all — I'll request the repo invite and the security questionnaire from the customer and tag everyone when I have it. :pray:
